properties.instruction_text: Check whether the pump starts when the air is turned on

evidence.text: * To determine if the fluid hose or gun is obstructed, follow the Pressure Relief Procedure on page 8. Disconnect the fluid hose and place a container at the pump fluid outlet to catch any fluid. Turn on the air just enough to start the pump (about 20–40 psi [0.14–0.3 MPa, 1.4–2.8 bar]). If the pump starts when the air is turned on, the obstruc- tion is in the fluid hose or gun.

conditions: To determine if the fluid hose or gun is obstructed

evidence.text: * To determine if the fluid hose or gun is obstructed, follow the Pressure Relief Procedure on page 8. Disconnect the fluid hose and place a container at the pump fluid outlet to catch any fluid. Turn on the air just enough to start the pump (about 20–40 psi [0.14–0.3 MPa, 1.4–2.8 bar]). If the pump starts when the air is turned on, the obstruc- tion is in the fluid hose or gun.
PROBLEM (same as row above): Pump fails to operate. | CAUSE: Obstructed fluid hose or gun/valve; fluid hose ID is too small. | SOLUTION: Clear*; use a hose with a larger ID.

PROBLEM (same as row above): Pump operates, but output is low on both strokes. | CAUSE: Obstructed fluid hose or gun/valve; fluid hose ID is too small. | SOLUTION: Clear*; use a hose with a larger ID.
